subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Ancient Automata: The First Robots
description: One-minute skill: Ancient Automata: The First Robots.

hook.text: In ancient Greece, Heron of Alexandria built a mechanical theater that performed plays without human actors.

buildup.text: His automata used falling weights, pulleys, and string to move figures, open doors, and pour wine on cue.

discovery.text: These machines followed a sequence — the world's first programs, written in rope and gears instead of code.

twist.text: Al-Jazari in the 1200s built water clocks with moving figures. His programmable drum machine predated computers by 700 years.

climax.text: These inventors proved that machines could imitate life. They planted the seed that grew into modern robotics.

punchline.text: Robots began as toys. The ambition behind them was anything but.

quiz.question: What powered Heron of Alexandria's mechanical theater?
options: Steam pressure from heated water tanks
Falling weights, pulleys, and string in a programmed sequence
Hand-cranked gears operated by hidden stagehands
